issue_context.title: SWC should parse `yield<T> (v: T)=>v`
comments:
Investigation: When JSX/TSX is enabled, this code can be correctly parsed.

CC @kdy1 Do you have any ideas?

I tried `cargo test --features debug 9914` and I found 

```
  DEBUG  try_parse_ts__success_value: Some(;)
    at crates/swc_ecma_parser/src/parser/typescript.rs:626
    in try_parse_ts with cur: Some(< (jsx tag start))
```

So I think it's lexed as a start tag for a jsx element.
This closed issue has been automatically locked because it had no new activity for a month. If you are running into a similar issue, please create a new issue with the steps to reproduce. Thank you.

review_comments: Does this mean we now produce `Token::JSXTagStart` even when `jsx()` is not enabled?

Actually, when we encounter `JSXTagStart`, it indicates that JSX is enabled. The current implementation has just one fewer condition compared to the previous code, but logically, it should be equivalent in functionality.

This code ended up in its current state due to my rebase and squash process. However, upon reviewing it, I realize this part doesn’t actually need to be changed. If needed, I’m happy to revert this change. Please let me know your thoughts!
I think the previous check is needless, as the existence of a such token proves `self.input.syntax().jsx() == true`. Thank you for clarification!
